status: MRI-only simple regression and same-sample Pearson correlation estimated; adjusted primary model not yet fitted.

design.slope_unit: Correct responses per 0.1 mm greater thickness

correlation.calibration: The analytic Pearson p-value has a bivariate-normal reference; non-normality and the undocumented sampling design limit its interpretation. The same-sample classical slope t test has the equivalent numeric p-value under its own linear-model assumptions.
correlation.scope: Recomputed on the 842-person common modeling sample; no reuse of the earlier 843-person Phase 2 result.

hypothesis_test.reporting: Report the two-sided nominal t-test p-value and 95% interval for the course simple-regression exercise; this is secondary to the adjusted estimand.
hypothesis_test.multiplicity: One primary Phase 4 coefficient test at alpha 0.05. Secondary and companion p-values are explicitly nominal; no familywise guarantee across coefficients, methods or phases is claimed. The separate completed Phase 3 Holm family remains unchanged.
hypothesis_test.relation_to_correlation: The Pearson and classical slope p-values are algebraically linked for this one-predictor intercept model; they are not two independent confirmations.

methods.estimator: Equal-weight OLS using economic pivoted QR and triangular solves, with coefficients returned to registered order; no explicit inversion of X'X.
methods.model_based_covariance: s^2 (X'X)^(-1), with s^2 = SSE/(n-p) and p including the intercept.
methods.coefficient_intervals: Individual two-sided 95% Student t intervals, estimate +/- t(0.975,n-p) SE. Exact t calibration requires the classical independent, homoskedastic normal-error linear model; otherwise qualifications are required.

hc3_companion.role: Prespecified companion coefficient uncertainty, reported alongside the model-based results regardless of diagnostic significance; never choose whichever gives a smaller p-value.
hc3_companion.reference_distribution: Use t with n-p degrees of freedom as an explicit finite-sample convention; HC3 interval/test calibration is approximate, not exact normal-theory t inference.
hc3_companion.limit: HC3 addresses coefficient covariance under heteroskedasticity; it does not correct nonlinearity, dependence, selection bias or source imputation uncertainty and does not supply a heteroskedastic individual prediction interval.

methods.interval_scope: Individual 95% intervals, not simultaneous or prediction intervals.
methods.numeric_tail_note: A zero computed coefficient p-value is flagged as numerical underflow, not interpreted as a literal zero probability.

identities: Slope equals r * sample_SD(score) / sample_SD(centered thickness per 0.1 mm)
Classical slope t equals r * sqrt((n-2)/(1-r^2))
Classical slope p matches Pearson p
SST equals SSE plus explained SS
Residuals sum to zero and are orthogonal to each model column
The hat-matrix trace equals the model rank
numeric_checks.limits: These checks establish computational consistency, not distributional validity or independent scientific replication.

interpretation.slope: The slope is an unadjusted between-person mean-score association per 0.1 mm greater left thickness within the eligible normal-cognition sample; it is not a within-person change or causal effect.
interpretation.intercept: The centered intercept is the fitted mean score at 2.344 mm, within the observed thickness range. This MRI-only model does not condition on age, recorded sex or education.
interpretation.evidence: The model-based slope interval includes zero; the HC3 companion interval includes zero. The nominal model-based test does not reject zero slope at the registered reference level. Read the effect and interval widths in score units. Non-rejection does not establish absence of an association or practical equivalence.
interpretation.p_value: Under the zero-slope null and the classical linear-model assumptions, the nominal p-value is the tail probability of a t statistic at least as far from zero as observed. It is not the probability that the null is true.
interpretation.fit: R-squared describes in-sample squared score variation accounted for by this linear thickness model; it is not external predictive accuracy or a causal fraction.
interpretation.hc3: The companion changes coefficient uncertainty, not the OLS line. Its t calibration is approximate; agreement does not remove sampling, functional-form or imputation limitations.
interpretation.remaining_work: Fit UDS-only and integrated models in Step 4 to answer the adjusted primary question. Residual/influence diagnostics and profile prediction intervals remain later work.

sampling_and_preparation.unit: One participant with the single supplied UDS record and the single supplied MRI record, joined one-to-one on NACCID.
sampling_and_preparation.target: The source population represented by this teaching extract, conditional on model_normal eligibility and the sampling/model assumptions; no claim of representativeness for all NACC participants.
sampling_and_preparation.independence: One supplied row per ID is verified; independence across people remains a modeling assumption.
sampling_and_preparation.selection: Random selection is reported, but its sampling frame, selection probabilities and source selection eligibility are undocumented.
sampling_and_preparation.source_preparation: The source preparation and imputation methods and value-level masks are unknown. Treat the supplied values as fixed inputs; this analysis cannot propagate additional imputation/preparation uncertainty.

visit_and_scan_timing.record_rule: Use the single supplied record per participant; no within-person visit selection is possible or performed.
visit_and_scan_timing.temporal_proximity: Unverifiable from the supplied files; do not assert baseline, first visit, nearest scan or contemporaneous measurements.
visit_and_scan_timing.track_c5_status: Participant-level input structure is documented. Temporal proximity remains unverified and would require authoritative metadata or course-team clarification.

sampling_and_preparation.scan_quality: Finite positive thickness establishes numerical usability, not scan-level quality control.

limitations.scope: Exploratory unadjusted inference. Model-based t calibration depends on the stated mean, independence, variance and error-distribution assumptions; count-scale coverage is approximate. HC3 does not establish a correct mean form or participant independence.
limitations.scale: The response is a count. No raw scores, fitted values or intervals are rounded or clipped to force the usable range.

figure.purpose: Observed score-thickness scatter and the MRI-only least-squares line over observed thickness support.
figure.privacy: No participant IDs or hover labels. All 842 observations are plotted without jitter or exclusions; overlapping observations may coincide.
figure.intervals: No prediction or mean-response ribbon is shown at this step.
